name: Bicep: storage insecure transport / weak TLS
attack_scenario: a network attacker on the path strips TLS or forces a downgrade to TLS1.0, then reads or tampers with blobs, access keys, and SAS tokens in transit
negative_test_hint: attempt to read a blob over "http://mystorageacct.blob.core.windows.net" and over a TLS1.0 handshake and assert the storage account rejects both, serving only HTTPS with TLS1_2 or newer

exemplar.explanation: supportsHttpsTrafficOnly:false lets clients reach the storage account over plaintext HTTP, and minimumTlsVersion TLS1_0/TLS1_1 keeps deprecated, downgradeable TLS enabled. Azure's secure default is HTTPS-only with TLS1_2 (CIS Azure Storage benchmark). Key/value is storage-specific ('TLS1_x' form), distinct from App Service minTlsVersion '1.x'.
